form: two turns: A commits to a voluntary, audacious, harmless act; B answers with laughter plus an admiring-class insult

items.insult: You are out of your mind.
items.a: I sold the car and put every cent into a food truck that sells nothing but grilled cheese. I pick it up Thursday.
items.b: [laughter] You are out of your mind.

items.a: I've been up at four every morning this month teaching myself accordion. I'm playing the farmers market on Saturday.
The landlord wanted six hundred to repaint, so I told him I'd do it myself. I started on the ceiling at eleven last night.
Remember the sourdough starter you said would never take? I entered a loaf in the county fair and it took first.
They had me on the karaoke list by mistake, so I did the whole song, key change and all. They made me do it twice.
I finished the forty-eight ounce steak in under an hour. Dinner was free and my picture's on the wall by the register now.
I've been mailing my brother one sock a week since June. He has not said a single word about it.
I drove six hours to surprise her at the airport, found out she'd landed in Denver, and got straight back in the car.
I ran the whole marathon in the hot dog costume. Beat my old time by nine minutes.
I sent them the application as a joke at two in the morning. They called this afternoon and offered me the job.
